title: BUG: schema_dsl() raises IndexError when a field has no name before the colon
body:
Calling `schema_dsl()` with a DSL string where a field has no name before the colon (e.g. `':description'` or `'name, :description'`) crashes with an `IndexError`. This is reachable from the CLI via `llm schema dsl ':foo'` and from `resolve_schema_input` whenever the schema string contains such a field.

Traceback:
```
File "llm/utils.py", line 395, in schema_dsl
    field_name = field_parts[0].strip()
                 ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
IndexError: list index out of range
```

Root cause: after `field.split(":", 1)`, the left side (`field_info`) is empty. `field_info.strip().split()` returns `[]`, so indexing `field_parts[0]` raises `IndexError`.

Minimal repro:
```python
from llm.utils import schema_dsl
schema_dsl(':just a description')  # IndexError
```
